what_this_is: A SIMULATION of skeletal-element patterning by a Bmp-Sox9-Wnt Turing network in a limb-bud-shaped domain. No value in this file is an observation, a measurement, or a reproduction of published data. The element counts, wavelengths and critical domain size are properties of this model at these parameters and nothing else.

model.name: BSW (Bmp-Sox9-Wnt) Turing network with a proximodistal Fgf gradient

variables.note: D_S = 0; Sox9 is cell-autonomous (sourced: onimaru2016 states the system has one non-diffusive molecule, Sox9).
static normalised gradient from the distal margin (the AER)

equations_latex.Sox9: \frac{\partial S}{\partial t} = \beta\left(k_2 B - k_3 W - S^3\right)
equations_latex.Bmp: \frac{\partial B}{\partial t} = \beta\left(\alpha_B - (1-k_F F)\,k_4 S - k_5 B + D_B \nabla^2 B\right)
equations_latex.Wnt: \frac{\partial W}{\partial t} = \beta\left(\alpha_W - k_7 k_F F\,S - k_9 W + D_W \nabla^2 W\right)
equations_latex.Fgf: F(\hat{x}) = F_{\max}\,e^{-g\,\hat{x}},\qquad \hat{x} = \frac{\text{distance proximal from the distal margin}}{L_{PD}}

topology.evidence: onimaru2016 eq (16), full-text; cubic self-damping, the only nonlinearity
onimaru2016 Results, 'repressing k4 and boosting k7', full-text
onimaru2016 Results, 'repressing k4 and boosting k7', full-text

parameters.name: beta
parameters.source: onimaru2016 Methods, 'Parameter values were beta=8, ...' for Figs 4-5
parameters.note: Global coefficient controlling the speed of pattern appearance.

parameters.name: k2
parameters.note: Bmp -> Sox9 activation strength. Onimaru et al. perturb exactly this parameter to represent Bmp inhibition.

parameters.name: k3
parameters.note: Wnt -| Sox9 inhibition strength (the minus sign is explicit in eq 16).

parameters.name: k4
parameters.note: Sox9 -| Bmp inhibition strength; repressed by Fgf.

parameters.name: k7
parameters.note: Sox9 -| Wnt inhibition strength; boosted by Fgf.

parameters.name: k5
parameters.note: Bmp linear decay.

parameters.name: k9
parameters.note: Wnt linear decay.

parameters.name: kF
parameters.note: Strength with which the normalised Fgf field F in [0,1] modulates k4 and k7.

parameters.name: D_B
parameters.note: Bmp diffusion. Bmp is the LONG-range species (D_B > D_W).

parameters.name: D_W
parameters.note: Wnt diffusion. Wnt is the SHORT-range species.

parameters.name: alpha_B
parameters.note: Constant Bmp production.

parameters.name: alpha_W
parameters.source: CHANGED from the published value alpha_W = 1.2 (onimaru2016 Methods).
parameters.note: alpha_W = k2*alpha_B*k9/(k3*k5) = 0.03333, chosen so the homogeneous steady state sits exactly at S*=0, where the cubic self-damping -3S*^2 vanishes and the paper's own LINEAR Turing conditions apply. With the published alpha_W = 1.2 my own linear stability analysis finds NO Turing instability anywhere on this static domain: see linear_stability.published_set_check in the JSON. This is the single substantive departure from the published parameter set and it is the reason the whole set must be read as 'published form, operating point retuned'.

parameters.name: F_max
parameters.source: no published value for this geometry
parameters.note: Distal maximum of the normalised Fgf field. Chosen just BELOW the upper edge of the Turing window in F (F_hopf, computed by the LSA below), so that no part of the bud sits in the uniform (q=0) instability regime. Calibration choice.

parameters.name: F_decay
parameters.source: onimaru2016 gives exp(-3*x) on a UNIT SQUARE (Supplementary Fig. 7); the fin/limb simulations instead solve a reaction-diffusion Fgf field whose absolute spatial scale is set by their mesh, which I do not have.
parameters.note: F(x_hat) = F_max * exp(-F_decay * x_hat), x_hat = normalised distance proximal from the distal margin. F_decay=4 (vs the published square-domain 3) makes the Turing-permissive band about one wavelength deep, which is what yields a single proximodistal row of elements rather than two rows.

parameters.name: L_PD
parameters.note: Proximodistal length of the paddle.

parameters.name: W_AP_half
parameters.note: Half-width of the paddle at its distal margin. L_PD and W_AP_half were chosen so that the WILD-TYPE-LIKE run yields about five elements. The five-element outcome is therefore IMPOSED by the domain, not predicted. What the model predicts is how the element count MOVES when the wavelength or the domain is changed.

parameters.name: dx
parameters.note: Grid spacing; checked by the grid-refinement arm.

parameters.name: dt
parameters.source: numerical choice (onimaru2016 use dt=0.002 with an explicit Heun solver; this script uses a semi-implicit solver, so a larger step is admissible)
parameters.note: Checked by the dt-refinement arm. dt=0.02 was measured to be numerically UNSTABLE here; dt=0.01, 0.005 and 0.002 agree to 5 significant figures.

parameters.name: T_end
parameters.note: The pattern coarsens after onset and the coarsening ARRESTS by t~40 (measured in a 1-D control out to t=320). T_end=60 is past arrest.

parameters.name: noise_amplitude
parameters.source: onimaru2016 use 1% Gaussian MULTIPLICATIVE noise at each step; multiplicative noise vanishes identically at this model's steady state S*=0, so it cannot be used here.
parameters.note: Seeded additive Gaussian perturbation of S at t=0, s.d. 1% of the Bmp steady state. A control arm adds dt-scaled per-step additive noise instead.

parameter_provenance_summary.statement: The EQUATION FORM and 11 of 19 parameters are sourced at full-text level from onimaru2016, which states that it implements the raspopovic2014 mouse BSW model. One sourced parameter (alpha_W) was CHANGED, for the reason recorded in its entry and measured in linear_stability.published_set_check. The geometry, the Fgf gradient shape, and all numerical parameters are assumed. The mouse parameter set of raspopovic2014 could not be obtained: that paper is subscription-only and was read at abstract level.

linear_stability.method: Eigenvalues of the 3x3 Jacobian M(q) of the full nonlinear system, linearised about the homogeneous steady state, with the diffusion terms -D_B q^2 and -D_W q^2 on the diagonal and D_S = 0, evaluated on a grid of 6001 wavenumbers q in [0, 1.2]. Turing instability is declared when max Re sigma(0) < 0 AND max_q Re sigma(q) > 0 at q > 0. The homogeneous steady states are the real roots of the cubic in S obtained by eliminating B and W.

turing_window_in_F.note: below F_low the uniform state is stable (no pattern); above F_high it is unstable at q=0 (uniform runaway, not a Turing pattern). F_max was set to 0.62, just below F_high.

published_set_check.question: Is the published parameter set, with alpha_W = 1.2, Turing-unstable on this static domain?
published_set_check.scope: 51 values of F in [0,1]; every real homogeneous steady state at each (1 to 3 roots); 6001 wavenumbers in [0,1.2].
published_set_check.diagnosis: With alpha_W = 1.2 the homogeneous steady state lies far from S = 0 (S* between about -5.8 and -0.58 on the branch that is continuous in F), so the cubic self-damping term -3S*^2 is large and suppresses the instability. The one state with a positive growth rate is unstable already at q = 0, which is a uniform instability, not a Turing instability.
published_set_check.what_this_does_and_does_not_mean: This is NOT a claim that the published model is wrong. onimaru2016 run it on a GROWING catshark fin mesh with per-step noise and a reaction-diffusion Fgf field whose absolute spatial scale is set by a mesh I do not have, and their published Turing-space analysis uses the LINEAR model (k1 = 0, so f_S = 0) with k3 = 1, not the cubic model with k3 = 3. My test is a static homogeneous domain and is not like-for-like. What it does mean is that I could not reproduce a Turing instability from the published numbers as I read them, so the operating point here is mine and is labelled assumed.

measured_wavelength.two_d_measurement: mean spacing between the anteroposterior centroids of adjacent counted elements, averaged over the 6 wild-type seeds. This is the pattern's own wavelength and it is the one used for the critical domain size.
measured_wavelength.one_d_uniform_control_note: 1-D periodic domain of length 1500 at a uniform Fgf level, spectral diffusion, probed at t=2 (still linear) and at t=160 (saturated). The three F values span the Turing-permissive band of the 2-D paddle.

comparison_to_linear_prediction.verdict: THEY DISAGREE, by a factor of about two, and the disagreement is reported rather than tuned away. The linear analysis predicts the FASTEST-GROWING mode at onset; the simulated pattern then coarsens and the coarsening arrests at a longer, nonlinearly selected wavelength. The agreement that does hold is in the LINEAR regime: a 1-D uniform-domain run probed at t = 2, while the amplitude is still small, has a dominant wavelength close to the LSA value (45 against 43 at F=0.62). Coarsening was measured to arrest by t ~ 40 and the wavelength was then unchanged out to t = 320. The 2-D measured spacing is shorter than the 1-D saturated wavelength at F = 0.62 because the 2-D permissive band spans a range of F, not just its distal maximum, and is only about one wavelength deep.

sweep_descriptions.diffusion_scale: D_B and D_W scaled together by this factor. lambda scales as sqrt(factor). This is the WAVELENGTH KNOB. Direction check: shorter wavelength should give MORE, thinner elements, which is the direction sheth2012 reports for progressive loss of distal Hox dose (read at abstract level; no number taken from it).
sweep_descriptions.fgf_strength_kF: Strength of the Fgf modulation of k4 and k7. Moves the system through the Turing window and changes where the permissive band sits.
sweep_descriptions.domain_scale: Linear scale factor on the whole paddle, Fgf gradient scaling with it. This is the bridge to a truncated limb bud.
sweep_descriptions.bmp_sox9_coupling_balanced: THIS IS THE CRITICALITY KNOB. k2 and alpha_W are scaled by the same factor, which changes the Bmp->Sox9 coupling strength while leaving the operating point exactly at S* = 0 (the balance k2*alpha_B/k5 = k3*alpha_W/k9 is preserved under a common factor, and S* = 0 was verified at every value). The linear-stability growth rate falls monotonically from factor 0.85 upwards and the Turing instability is LOST at factor 5.5 (max Re sigma over all q and all F in the bud becomes negative). Above that the field stays at the homogeneous steady state: a uniform Sox9 field and no skeletal elements, with no change to the domain and no change to the wavelength mechanism.
sweep_descriptions.bmp_to_sox9_k2_alone: Strength of Bmp activation of Sox9, varied ON ITS OWN. onimaru2016 perturb exactly this parameter to represent Bmp inhibition. READ THIS ONE WITH CARE and prefer bmp_sox9_coupling_balanced: in this retuned model the homogeneous steady state sits at S* = 0 only when k2*alpha_B/k5 = k3*alpha_W/k9, which with the other values here means only at k2 = 1. Changing k2 alone therefore moves the operating point as well as the coupling, and the two effects cannot be separated. That is why every value except 1 collapses to a single fused domain. The sweep is kept because that fragility is a real property of the assumed operating point and hiding it would misrepresent the model.
sweep_descriptions.wnt_production_alphaW_scale: Multiplier on alpha_W, the constant Wnt production term. READ THIS ONE WITH CARE. onimaru2016 perturb Wnt production and report partial fusion of Sox9 into continuous domains, matched in vivo by a porcupine inhibitor, and that is what the fused class here looks like. BUT in this retuned model alpha_W also sets the operating point: S* = 0 only at the one value alpha_W = k2*alpha_B*k9/(k3*k5), and moving alpha_W moves S* away from zero, which switches the cubic self-damping -3S*^2 back on. So this sweep measures the FRAGILITY OF THE ASSUMED OPERATING POINT at least as much as it measures a Wnt perturbation, and the two cannot be separated in this parameterisation. It is reported because that fragility is a real and unflattering property of the choice made here, not because it is a clean perturbation.

one_condition_behind_every_route_to_no_e.statement: In this model every route to zero skeletal elements is the same geometric condition: the Turing-PERMISSIVE REGION must be at least about one wavelength across. Shrinking the bud shrinks that region in space; de-tuning the network shrinks it in parameter space, and therefore also in space, because the Fgf gradient maps parameter space onto the proximodistal axis.
one_condition_behind_every_route_to_no_e.evidence_from_the_domain_sweep: Elements disappear below about 0.9 wavelengths of anteroposterior width.
one_condition_behind_every_route_to_no_e.evidence_from_the_coupling_sweep: At Bmp-Sox9 coupling x5 the linear analysis still reports a Turing instability (max growth +0.31 per time unit), but the simulation forms nothing. The reason is geometric and is computable from the LSA: at that coupling the Turing window has narrowed to F in (0.596, 1.0), and with F_max = 0.62 and F = F_max*exp(-4*x_hat) over L_PD = 300, the permissive strip is only about 3.0 model length units deep, against a wavelength of 18.6 there - under a fifth of a wavelength, and narrower than one grid cell. At coupling x4 the strip is about 13.7 units against a wavelength of 24.9, roughly 0.55 wavelengths, and the counts are correspondingly marginal and seed-dependent (1, 3, 1).
one_condition_behind_every_route_to_no_e.consequence: The simulated loss of pattern (coupling x5) comes BEFORE the formal loss of linear instability (x5.5). Both numbers are reported; the simulated one is the one that would be observable.

critical_domain_size.axis: anteroposterior width of the paddle at its widest point
critical_domain_size.definition: Midpoint between the largest domain scale with a mean element count of exactly zero and the smallest with a non-zero mean, expressed in units of the measured wavelength lambda_meas. The uncertainty is half that interval and is set by the spacing of the domain_scale grid, not by a fit.
critical_domain_size.rule_sensitivity: THE CRITICAL SIZE DEPENDS ON THE COUNTING RULE, by about a factor of two, and both numbers are given. The revised rule requires a surviving component to be at least 0.10 * lambda_meas^2; the original required only 0.10 * lambda_lin^2, which is about four times smaller in area and so still counts a partial condensation in a bud too small to hold a whole one. Quote the range, not one end of it.
critical_domain_size.reading: Somewhere between about half a wavelength and about one and a quarter wavelengths of anteroposterior width, the paddle stops being able to hold an element and the field is unpatterned. Because the Fgf gradient scales with the bud, the proximodistal permissive band shrinks at the same time, so both axes run out together; the AP figure is the one quoted and the PD extent at the same point is given beside it.

no_reaction.what: Sox9->Bmp and Sox9->Wnt couplings and the Bmp/Wnt->Sox9 terms all set to zero; diffusion, production and decay left in place.

no_initial_perturbation.what: full model, but the t=0 perturbation of S is omitted, so the field starts at the exact homogeneous steady state (verified analytically: S*=0, B*=alpha_B/k5, W*=alpha_W/k9 makes all three time derivatives vanish at every point, whatever the local Fgf level).
no_initial_perturbation.result: DID NOT STAY FLAT, and this is reported rather than quietly dropped.
no_initial_perturbation.interpretation: The state is linearly UNSTABLE with max growth rate 8.18 per model time unit, and the run is 60 time units long, so double-precision rounding at the 1e-16 level is amplified by roughly exp(490) and saturates long before the end. A linearly unstable state cannot be held flat numerically, so this arm cannot test what it was designed to test. What it DOES establish is the converse: the pattern is not an artifact of the injected noise, because it forms without any. The arm that genuinely tests flatness is no_reaction (which passed), and the sub-critical end of bmp_sox9_coupling_balanced, which is linearly stable and does stay flat.

per_step_noise.what: dt-scaled additive Gaussian noise on S at every step instead of a single t=0 perturbation (the published scheme is 1% multiplicative noise per step, which vanishes identically at S*=0).
per_step_noise.must_show: the same element counts as the default noise model

positive_and_negative_control_for_the_co.what: The counter is run against a case it must flag and a case it must not: the wild-type-like field (must return a multi-element count) and the no-reaction field (must return 0).

classification_rule: Applied to the Sox9 field S at t = T_end, on the masked domain. (1) AMPLITUDE GATE: if p99(S) - p1(S) < 0.05 model concentration units, or p99(S) <= 0, the field is called unpatterned, element_count = 0, class = 'none'. (2) THRESHOLD: Sox9-high = {S > 0.25 * p99(S)}. The homogeneous steady state is S* = 0 by construction, so this threshold is referenced to the known unpatterned baseline and the unpatterned background can never be counted as an element. (3) MINIMUM SIZE: connected components (4-connectivity) of the Sox9-high set with area >= 0.10 * lambda_elem^2 are counted as elements, where lambda_elem = lambda_meas_WT * lambda_lin(condition) / lambda_lin(WT): the wavelength MEASURED in the wild-type runs, carried to each condition by that condition's analytic linear-stability wavelength. It uses no measurement from the run being counted. (4) CLASS from the count n: n=0 -> 'none'; n=1 -> 'single element', or 'single fused domain' if that one component spans more than 70% of the anteroposterior width; 2<=n<=4 -> 'reduced'; n=5 -> 'normal digit number'; n>=6 -> 'increased (polydactyl-like)'.
classification_rule_change: The rule was declared before any sweep was run, and step (3) originally used lambda_lin(condition) itself rather than lambda_elem. It was CHANGED after the first full run, and the change is recorded here rather than quietly made. The reason is a defect in the specification, not a result I disliked: the linear-stability wavelength is about half the wavelength the saturated pattern actually has (measured, and reported under measured_wavelength), so a minimum area of 0.10 * lambda_lin^2 is four times too small and admits slivers at the anterior and posterior ends of the band as if they were elements. Every element count under the ORIGINAL rule is kept alongside, as element_counts_linear_rule in each sweep row and as sweeps_under_the_original_rule.wild_type. Under the original rule the wild-type count was [5, 7, 6, 5, 5, 4] (mean 5.33); under the revised rule it is [5, 4, 5, 4, 4, 3] (mean 4.17). The qualitative shape of every sweep is the same under both.

sweeps_under_the_original_rule.note: Per-condition counts under the original rule are in each sweep row as element_counts_linear_rule.

seeds.note: Turing patterns are seed-dependent. Every sweep point is run from 3 fixed seeds and the spread is reported as element_count_sd; the individual counts are kept in element_counts.

numerics.scheme: IMEX. Diffusion and linear decay of B and W implicit (one sparse LU factorisation per condition, reused every step); the cubic in S treated semi-implicitly as -S_new * S_old^2, which keeps S bounded; all couplings explicit. Zero-flux boundary on the masked domain.
numerics.deviation_from_published_numerics: onimaru2016 use an explicit Heun solver with dt = 0.002 on a triangular finite-volume mesh and a growing domain. This is a fixed cartesian grid, a static domain, and a semi-implicit solver.
numerics.dt_0.02_was_unstable: Measured: at dt = 0.02 the solution diverged to ~1e8; at dt = 0.01, 0.005 and 0.002 the final field agreed to 5 significant figures. dt = 0.01 is the default.

limitations: NO GROWTH. The real limb bud grows while it patterns, and raspopovic2014's and onimaru2016's simulations both run on growing meshes. On a static domain the elements form as condensations in a distal band rather than elongating into proximodistally running digit rays. This study measures element NUMBER, not element SHAPE, and the shapes here should not be read as digit morphology.
The five-element wild-type-like outcome is IMPOSED by the chosen paddle width, not predicted. Only the changes in element count across the sweeps are model predictions.

The mouse parameter set of raspopovic2014 was not obtainable. The numbers used come from onimaru2016's CATSHARK FIN simulation of the same network, and one of them (alpha_W) had to be changed to obtain a Turing instability at all.

All lengths are model length units. The model as published carries no physical length scale that I can verify, so no result here is in micrometres and no statement is made about the real size of any limb bud.
The linear-stability wavelength and the simulated wavelength differ by a factor of about two (see measured_wavelength). The simulated value is the one used for the critical domain size.

The classification into phenotype classes is a threshold rule on a simulated scalar field. It is objective and pre-declared, but 'normal digit number' here means 'five counted components in this simulation', not a mouse phenotype.
Only one noise model, one domain shape, and one gradient shape were explored. Turing element counts are sensitive to all three.

THE ASSUMED OPERATING POINT IS FRAGILE. Because the steady state was placed at S* = 0 by balancing k2*alpha_B/k5 against k3*alpha_W/k9, any parameter change that breaks that balance moves S* off zero and switches the cubic self-damping back on. A 20% change in alpha_W alone, or a 15% change in k2 alone, collapses the five-element pattern to a single fused domain (see the wnt_production_alphaW_scale and bmp_to_sox9_k2_alone sweeps). The bmp_sox9_coupling_balanced sweep exists because it changes the coupling WITHOUT breaking that balance, and it is the one to read for criticality. The fragility is a property of this reparameterisation, not a claim about the published model.

THE ELEMENT COUNT DEPENDS ON THE MINIMUM-SIZE CUT by about one element, because the anterior-most and posterior-most condensations sit where the paddle narrows and are genuinely smaller. The wild-type count is 5.3 +/- 0.9 under the original rule and 4.2 +/- 0.7 under the revised one, over the same six seeds, and the critical domain size moves by about a factor of two between them. Treat one element as the resolution of this measurement.
The grid-refinement arm changes the element count by 1 in two of three conditions, which is the same one-element resolution; the dt-refinement arm changes nothing.
what_this_does_not_establish: It does not establish that any real limbless or limb-reduced animal, or any real mutant, lacks limbs because of a change in a Turing wavelength or a sub-critical patterning system. No animal was measured here.
It does not establish that the BSW network is the correct mechanism of mouse digit patterning. That is raspopovic2014's claim, read here at abstract level only.
It does not reproduce any published figure. No comparison to published data was made, so no agreement with data is claimed.
A simulated phenotype class is not a phenotype.

sources.used_for: The claim that a Bmp-Sox9-Wnt Turing network drives mouse digit specification and is modulated by morphogen gradients. This is the model this script implements; the equations themselves were taken at full-text level from onimaru2016, which states that it implements this model.

sources.citation: Sheth R, Marcon L, Bastida MF, Junco M, Quintana L, Dahn R, Kmita M, Sharpe J, Ros MA (2012) Hox genes regulate digit patterning by controlling the wavelength of a Turing-type mechanism. Science 338(6113):1476-1480.
sources.how_checked: PMID and DOI resolved through the PubMed MCP tool. PMC4486416 is a PMC Canada author manuscript: the PubMed full-text tool returned an EMPTY body, the Europe PMC fullTextXML endpoint returned HTTP 500, the rendered PDF returned HTTP 403, and NCBI efetch db=pmc returned front matter with no <body>. Only the abstract was read.
sources.used_for: The DIRECTION of the wavelength sweep only: progressive loss of distal Hox dose gives progressively more, thinner, densely packed digits, i.e. a shorter Turing wavelength. No quantitative value is taken from this paper.

sources.citation: Onimaru K, Marcon L, Musy M, Tanaka M, Sharpe J (2016) The fin-to-limb transition as the re-organization of a Turing pattern. Nat Commun 7:11582.
sources.how_checked: Full text XML retrieved from the Europe PMC REST endpoint (/PMC4879262/fullTextXML, HTTP 200, 120161 bytes) on 2026-11-01, and the Methods section read. Equations (16)-(19) are published as images; the image files ncomms11582-m22..m25.jpg were downloaded from the PMC CDN and read directly. Parameter values were read verbatim from the Methods paragraph 'Mathematical analysis and numerical simulation'.
sources.used_for: The equation form and every sourced numeric parameter below. This paper states in its own text that it uses 'the BSW model' of Raspopovic et al. 2014 (its reference 12) and that the Fgf gradient modulates the same parameters as in the mouse model, 'repressing k4 and boosting k7'. It also supplies the numerical recipe (Heun, dt=0.002, zero-flux, homogeneous steady-state initial condition, 1% Gaussian multiplicative noise per step) and the simple square-domain Fgf substitute exp(-3x) on 0<=x<=1.
sources.caveat: Onimaru et al. apply this parameter set to a GROWING catshark pectoral fin mesh, where Sox9 forms spots. It is the same network as the mouse model but not the mouse parameter set, which was not obtainable (see raspopovic2014).

runtime_note: runtime_seconds is for THIS invocation. When the figures are redrawn from the cached simulation results (--figures) it does not include the simulations. The cached results came from a full run of 179 simulations on 5 worker processes, 437.0 s of wall clock to the end of the sweeps on a shared 8-core host.
